title: South by West; or, Winter in the Rocky Mountains and Spring in Mexico
summary: Rose Kingsley (1845–1925), a daughter of Charles Kingsley, who edited the book and wrote its preface, crossed the Atlantic in the autumn of 1871 with the family of the Dean of Chester, who was attending the Episcopal Church Convention at Baltimore. She then went west by rail to join her brother in Colorado and spent the winter of 1871–72 at Colorado Springs, a new town at the foot of Pike’s Peak: its building and settlers, housekeeping in a shanty, rides into the cañons.

In the spring of 1872 she went by the Pacific Railroad to San Francisco and by steamer to Manzanillo, and travelled by coach and on horseback through Colima, Guadalajara and Querétaro to the city of Mexico during a revolt against the government, and on to Vera Cruz. Most of the book is letters and journal entries. Two chapters describe the resources of Colorado and of Mexico.
